## Trial `dns-forwarding-ubuntu24__BDwRAmD`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** node1 was configured as an authoritative-plus-forwarding DNS resolver scoped to the 10.100.10.0/24 network, answering inventory.internal with node2's address and forwarding everything else upstream. node2 and node3 were both switched to use node1 as DNS server via a persistent systemd-networkd override. All functional claims are backed by direct dig/resolvectl evidence, re-verified after each node's individual reboot with changed boot IDs consistent with fixed lifecycle snapshots. No unnecessary mutations or hygiene issues found.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.950 | 0.950 | 41/1 (+10 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **req-1 — Satisfied:** node1 becomes the DNS resolver for the shared private network, listening/serving scoped to it
  - **Why:** VyOS service dns forwarding configured with listen-address 10.100.10.10 and allow-from 10.100.10.0/24; committed and saved. pdns-recursor confirmed active and listening on 10.100.10.10:53 both before and after reboot.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-7054e32dadc54003`, `cmd-33c4368d4b2a4d8b`, `cmd-7fa88a88828b462e`, `cmd-93ad6b2a2c964aa4`
- **req-2 — Satisfied:** node1 answers inventory.internal with node2's address on the shared network
  - **Why:** authoritative-domain inventory.internal record a @ -> 10.100.10.11 (node2's confirmed IP) was set and committed; dig confirms this both pre- and post-reboot, and resolvectl on node2/node3 independently confirms the same result.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-7054e32dadc54003`, `cmd-33c4368d4b2a4d8b`, `cmd-37fc74f4a54947b1`, `cmd-e351c1da49e346af`, `cmd-b874afe27c814821`, `cmd-93ad6b2a2c964aa4`
- **req-3 — Satisfied:** node1 forwards all other queries upstream
  - **Why:** name-server 1.1.1.1 and 9.9.9.9 configured as forwarders; dig for example.com resolves to real public IPs both before and after node1's reboot.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-7054e32dadc54003`, `cmd-33c4368d4b2a4d8b`, `cmd-93ad6b2a2c964aa4`
- **req-4 — Satisfied:** node2 and node3 configured to resolve DNS through node1
  - **Why:** A systemd-networkd drop-in (DNS=10.100.10.10, UseDNS=no) was applied on both nodes; resolvectl shows current DNS server 10.100.10.10 with inventory.internal and example.com resolving correctly, confirmed again after each node's own reboot.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-55de619883cc431d`, `cmd-ab4c4406a8404df6`, `cmd-e351c1da49e346af`, `cmd-b874afe27c814821`, `cmd-36c4ef314f0d4858`, `cmd-1fe9d09ef60847dc`
